extracted.intended_audience: readers, critics, and aspiring poets interested in epic poetry (esp. Milton's Paradise Lost)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and critical observations for composing and judging epic poetry, illustrated through commentary on Milton's Paradise Lost (e.g., character-appropriateness, allegory, economy of description, probability of imagery).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate agent for the poem's central project
rubrics_metrics.description: The Prince of the fallen Angels was the only proper Person to give it Birth, and that the next to him in Dignity was the fittest to second and support it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major projects or proposals within an epic should be voiced by characters whose rank, temperament, and role make them the natural originators; choosing the right speaker lends plausibility and moral/psychological weight to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce the central project early
rubrics_metrics.description: It was just not to omit in the First Book the Project upon which the whole Poem turns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the poem's central enterprise or theme early (e.g., in Book I) so readers understand the poem's purpose and the subsequent episodes have clear relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use prophetic/pre-existence scenes to elevate subject
rubrics_metrics.description: There is something wonderfully Beautiful, and very apt to affect the Readers Imagination in this ancient Prophecy or Report in Heavn, concerning the Creation of Man... They are represented to have been the Talk of Heaven, before they were created.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Glimpses of pre-existence or prophetic discussion can magnify the dignity of the subject (here, mankind) and make their creation seem momentous; such devices should be used to honor the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublimity in large assemblies and grand scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: The rising of this great Assembly is described in a very Sublime and Poetical Manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mass scenes (assemblies, councils, hosts) should be rendered with grandeur and sublimity appropriate to their scale, using cadence and imagery that convey vastness and awe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of diversions to characters' dispositions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Diversions are every way suitable to Beings who had nothing left them but Strength and Knowledge misapplied. Such are their Contentions at the Race, and in Feats of Arms...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small episodes, entertainments, or diversions within the poem should reflect the nature and resources of the characters (e.g., fallen angels entertain themselves by feats of strength/arms), avoiding incongruous actions that break verisimilitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music and discourse should reflect theme and character
rubrics_metrics.description: Their Musick is employed in celebrating their own criminal Exploits, and their Discourse in sounding the unfathomable Depths of Fate, Free-will and Fore-knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Songs, speeches, and debates ought to serve characterisation and theme—here, celebrating crimes and debating metaphysical topics suits fallen angels; lyrical or rhetorical elements should not be ornamental but meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of description: concise lines can be more powerful
rubrics_metrics.description: The monstrous Animals produced in that Infernal World are represented by a single Line, which gives us a more horrid Idea of them, than a much longer Description would have done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sometimes a brief, striking line or image conveys horror or grandeur more effectively than extended description; prefer concentrated, suggestive phrasing when it intensifies effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use episodic material to refresh, not to distract
rubrics_metrics.description: This Episode of the fallen Spirits, and their Place of Habitation, comes in very happily to unbend the Mind of the Reader from its Attention to the Debate. An ordinary Poet would indeed have spun out so many Circumstances to a great Length, and by that means have weakned, instead of illustrated, the principal Fable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digressions or episodes should relieve reader fatigue and illuminate the main story; avoid over-spinning incidental material that dilutes the central fable or argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegory can be a finished piece but must fit the epic
rubrics_metrics.description: I have already declared my Opinion of the Allegory concerning Sin and Death, which is however a very finished Piece in its kind, when it is not considered as a Part of an Epic Poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegorical set-pieces may succeed on their own terms but the poet must consider how such concentrated allegory integrates with the scale and demands of an epic; assess whether it enhances or distracts from epic cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delicacy and naturalness of genealogical symbolism
rubrics_metrics.description: The Genealogy of the several Persons is contrived with great Delicacy. Sin is the Daughter of Satan, and Death the Offspring of Sin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbolic family relationships and origin stories should feel naturally motivated and psychologically/ethically convincing so that the allegory carries moral force rather than feeling arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence of symbolic roles and motivations
rubrics_metrics.description: How naturally the three Persons concerned in this Allegory are tempted by one common Interest to enter into a Confederacy together, and how properly Sin is made the Portress of Hell, and the only Being that can open the Gates to that World of Tortures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign symbolic functions in ways that cohere—characters' roles (e.g., portress, gate-opener) should follow logically from their nature and shared motives so that the allegory reads as integrated design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powerful descriptive details and sublime pictorial moments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Figure of Death, [the Regal Crown upon his Head,] his Menace of Satan, his advancing to the Combat, the Outcry at his Birth, are Circumstances too noble to be past over in Silence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include vivid, emblematic details (regal crown, menace, dramatic action) that produce memorable pictorial moments and elevate the scene's nobility or terror.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical sequencing and justness of thought in allegory
rubrics_metrics.description: The Justness of Thought which is observed in the Generation of these several Symbolical Persons; that Sin was produced upon the first Revolt of Satan, that Death appear'd soon after he was cast into Hell, and that the Terrors of Conscience were conceived at the Gate of this Place of Torments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegorical causation and chronology should be plausible and morally intelligible—readers should perceive a reasoned connection between revolt, sin, death, and conscience to sustain the allegory's force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting descriptions should be poetical and true to the poet's spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Description of the Gates is very poetical, as the opening of them is full of Milton's Spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topographical or architectural descriptions (gates, thresholds) should be rendered poetically in a manner consistent with the poet's voice and thematic concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer plausible, probable imagery among imaginative wonders
rubrics_metrics.description: I am pleased most with those Passages in this Description which carry in them a greater Measure of Probability, and are such as might possibly have happened. Of this kind is his first mounting in the Smoke... his falling into a Cloud of Nitre... springing upward like a Pyramid of Fire...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even in fantastical contexts, favor scenes that contain a sense of physical or causal plausibility; such grounded passages enhance reader belief and engagement amidst imaginative spectacle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use luminous cosmic imagery to produce beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: The Glimmering Light which shot into the Chaos from the utmost Verge of the Creation, with the distant discovery of the Earth that hung close by the Moon, are wonderfully Beautiful and Poetical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic cosmic or luminous images (glimmering light, distant Earth near the Moon) can yield striking beauty; employ such images to arrest the imagination and convey the scale of the poem.
